input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph 9(h) is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control clause anywhere in the Agreement. It gives AP the affiliate and successor freedom we want, but it extends the identical no-consent carve-out to Kubient, so Kubient can transfer the Agreement to any affiliate or acquirer — including an AP competitor — without our consent, which defeats the fallback requirement that all non-successor assignments be consent-gated and fails the preferred position's Vendor-side restrictions. Our edit keeps our own carve-out and the mutual reasonable-consent standard verbatim, limits the no-consent exception to AP, bars assignment to an AP competitor, and confirms that a change of control of AP gives Kubient no termination right (the existing post-Initial-Term notice right is a separate convenience issue and is not addressed here).

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
mappings.quote: without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld

mappings.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.

proposal.summary: Limit the no-consent assignment carve-out to Customer, bar Kubient assignment to a Customer competitor, and confirm no termination right on Customer's change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We keep our affiliate/successor assignment freedom but limit the no-consent carve-out to AP, so Kubient's assignments remain subject to our consent (which we will not unreasonably withhold) and can never be made to an AP competitor; we also confirm a change of control of AP gives Kubient no termination right.

ops.oldText: provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
ops.newText: provided however, that Customer may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction, Kubient may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Customer, and Customer's change of control shall not give Kubient any right to terminate this Agreement.
